style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></munderover><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">log</mi><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">p</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">y</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">t</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" lspace="0em" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">I</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">y</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">&lt;</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">t</mi></mrow></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" lspace="0em" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{gen}}(x,y)=-|y|^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{|y|}\log p_{\theta}(y_{t}\mid I,x,y_{&lt;t}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.4" class="ltx_p">The two paths therefore share the vision encoder and all backbone parameters but use task-appropriate outputs: retrieval stops after multimodal prefill and applies <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">W</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">e</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{e}</annotation></semantics></math> once, whereas generation applies the language-modeling head throughout autoregressive decoding. For training, the baseline combines the two task losses through a weighted objective, <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}=\lambda_{\mathrm{emb}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{emb}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{gen}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{gen}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">ℒ</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">λ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">emb</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">ℒ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">emb</mi></msub></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">+</mo><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">λ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">gen</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">ℒ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">gen</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}=\lambda_{\mathrm{emb}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{emb}}+\lambda_{\mathrm{gen}}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{gen}}</annotation></semantics></math>. This shared-backbone formulation enables compact joint training, but simply combining the task losses leaves visual-evidence allocation and interference between shared-parameter updates unresolved, as discussed in Section <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Conflicts Under Shared Capacity ‣ 2. Unified Multimodal Models: Formulation and Tensions ‣ WePM: Hierarchical Conflict Reconciliation for Unified MLLMs Unified Pocket Models for In-App Multimodal Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">2.2  Conflicts Under Shared Capacity</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unifying heterogeneous tasks—such as representation, generation, and decision—within a compact shared backbone introduces two fundamental difficulties. First, the three capabilities require visual evidence at different spatial granularities, despite sharing the same limited visual-token budget. Second, their training data are typically collected in separate task-specific corpora. Existing unified training recipes therefore commonly alternate among task-specific batches, causing consecutive updates to optimize different output semantics over the same backbone parameters. We trace these two difficulties to a granularity conflict in the retained evidence and an optimization conflict in the shared parameter updates.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Granularity conflict—which visual evidence should be retained? Representation may rely on global semantics for broad retrieval, but distinguishing hard negatives often requires regional attributes and fine details. Generation similarly combines scene-level context with localized evidence for OCR and detail-centric question answering, while decision may depend on either global state or local text, values, and regions specified by its schema. Because all three capabilities operate under a visual-token budget of at most <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>, uniformly compressing an image can preserve evidence useful to one task while discarding evidence required by another. The first challenge is therefore to preserve task-relevant evidence at multiple granularities within a single fixed token budget.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The second difficulty arises during optimization. Let <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{T}=\{\mathrm{emb},\mathrm{gen},\mathrm{dec}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">𝒯</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">emb</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">gen</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">dec</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{T}=\{\mathrm{emb},\mathrm{gen},\mathrm{dec}\}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}=\nabla_{\theta}\mathcal{L}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">g</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">θ</mi></msub><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">ℒ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}=\nabla_{\theta}\mathcal{L}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the gradient of task <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> with respect to the shared parameters. Under task-alternating training, an update using task <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> changes the loss of another task <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> according to</p>
<table id="S2.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{j}(\theta-\alpha g_{i})=\mathcal{L}_{j}(\theta)-\alpha\langle g_{j},g_{i}\rangle+O(\alpha^{2})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">ℒ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">θ</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">−</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">g</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">ℒ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">θ</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">−</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">g</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">g</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">+</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">α</mi><mn style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">2</mn></msup><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{j}(\theta-\alpha g_{i})=\mathcal{L}_{j}(\theta)-\alpha\langle g_{j},g_{i}\rangle+O(\alpha^{2}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">for sufficiently small <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">α</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">&gt;</mo><mn style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. When <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\langle g_{j},g_{i}\rangle&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">g</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">g</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">&lt;</mo><mn style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle g_{j},g_{i}\rangle&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, improving task <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> locally increases the loss of task <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, yielding direct directional interference. Even when the inner product is nonnegative, unequal gradient norms and update frequencies can allow one task to dominate the shared parameters. There are two natural approaches to mitigating this interference, but each exposes a distinct challenge.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Supervision conflict—can task-specific data be converted into paired supervision? One possible approach is to annotate every input with targets for all capabilities, so that representation, generation, and decision can be optimized from semantically aligned examples. Constructing such data at scale, however, is expensive and often fundamentally ambiguous. For example, a representation query such as “a small red flower” specifies a meaningful retrieval target but does not determine a unique generation response. Both “a small red flower blooms on the hillside” and “a small red flower grows in the woods” are plausible continuations. Assigning either response as the sole target introduces an arbitrary interpretation rather than genuine cross-task supervision. More generally, relevance relations, open-ended sequences, and typed decision labels define different target spaces and cannot always be converted into one another through hard annotations. The supervision challenge is therefore to obtain complementary cross-task learning signals without requiring exhaustive paired data or imposing a unique target where none exists.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Magnitude conflict—which task determines the shared update? An alternative to constructing fully paired data is to integrate gradients from different task-specific batches into one logical update. However, gradient integration alone does not ensure balanced task influence. For <math id="S2.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">n</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> batches of task <math id="S2.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, coefficient <math id="S2.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">λ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, and mean gradient <math id="S2.SS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">g</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">¯</mo></mover><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, the resulting update is</p>
<table id="S2.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\mathrm{joint}}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\lambda_{i}\sum_{b=1}^{n_{i}}\nabla_{\theta}\ell_{i,b}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}n_{i}\lambda_{i}\bar{g}_{i}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">g</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">joint</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">∈</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">𝒯</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">λ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">b</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">1</mn></mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">n</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub></munderover><mrow><msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">θ</mi></msub><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">b</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">∈</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">𝒯</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">n</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">λ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">g</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">¯</mo></mover><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" lspace="0em" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\mathrm{joint}}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}\lambda_{i}\sum_{b=1}^{n_{i}}\nabla_{\theta}\ell_{i,b}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{T}}n_{i}\lambda_{i}\bar{g}_{i}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.p5.2" class="ltx_p">The effective contribution of task <math id="S2.SS2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> is therefore determined jointly by its native gradient magnitude, its coefficient <math id="S2.SS2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">λ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, and its exposure frequency <math id="S2.SS2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">n</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. These quantities are not naturally comparable across heterogeneous objectives: representation losses are typically reduced over queries or candidate sets, generation losses over supervised tokens, and decision losses over typed instances. Their data pools may also differ substantially in size, causing some tasks to be sampled more frequently than others. Consequently, equal coefficients do not imply equal influence, and equal exposure does not imply balanced updates. A task with a larger effective contribution can dominate the joint gradient and overwrite capabilities learned from other tasks, even when their gradient directions are not directly opposed. Conversely, suppressing that contribution too aggressively can prevent the task from learning sufficiently. The magnitude conflict therefore lies in the mismatch between each task’s numerically induced optimization strength and its intended importance in the final capability trade-off. The challenge is to control both task weighting and task exposure so that the joint update reflects a deliberate balance rather than incidental differences in loss normalization, annotation density, or corpus size.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">These conflicts motivate the three corresponding components of WePM. MGVB reconciles heterogeneous evidence requirements within a shared visual-token budget. ULKD supplies cross-capability soft supervision without requiring unique hard targets or exhaustively paired annotations. SEMO controls the effective contribution of each task through explicit loss coefficients and task exposure, while using memory-efficient sequential accumulation to realize the specified joint update.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section" style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_section">3.  WePM: A Pocket Model for Heterogeneous On-Device Intelligence</h2>

<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.27365v1/final_fig/last_1109.png" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/244;" width="476" height="244" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Overview of WePM. A shared vision encoder and multimodal backbone produce task-appropriate outputs: normalized embeddings for representation, autoregressive responses for generation, and schema-conditioned scores for typed decision. MGVB allocates a fixed visual-token budget across global, regional, and fine-grained banks using the available textual context. During training, ULKD supplements representation and generation data with token-level generation guidance, candidate-list preferences, and representation alignment from capability-specific teachers. SEMO controls each task’s contribution through explicit loss weights and exposure schedules, while sequential gradient accumulation executes the joint update within training-memory constraints.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">3.1  Multi-Granularity Visual Budgeting</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Representation, generation, and visually grounded decision require evidence at different spatial scales. Coarse-grained retrieval is largely governed by global scene semantics, whereas discriminating hard negatives often requires object-level and relational cues. OCR and detail-centric visual question answering depend on localized evidence that may occupy only a few image patches, while a decision may depend on either global state or a local value specified by its criteria. Under a fixed visual-token budget, uniform compression inevitably preserves redundant information at some scales while discarding evidence critical at others. We therefore introduce the <em id="S3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Multi-Granularity Visual Budgeting</em>, which explicitly distributes the available visual capacity across global, regional, and fine-grained representations.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Given spatially indexed features <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X=\{x_{j}\}_{j=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">1</mn></mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">N</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X=\{x_{j}\}_{j=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> produced by a single vision-encoder forward pass, MGVB constructs three complementary token banks:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V=[V_{g};V_{r};V_{f}],\qquad B_{g}+B_{r}+B_{f}=B," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">V</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">V</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">g</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">;</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">V</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">r</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">;</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">V</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">f</mi></msub></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">B</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">g</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">+</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">B</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">r</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">+</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">B</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">f</mi></msub></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">B</mi></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V=[V_{g};V_{r};V_{f}],\qquad B_{g}+B_{r}+B_{f}=B,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">B</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">B</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{r}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">B</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the token budgets of the global, regional, and fine-grained banks, respectively, and <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> is the total number of visual tokens supplied to the language backbone. The global bank employs learned latent queries to aggregate image-level semantics. The regional bank summarizes candidate regions, preserving object identities, spatial layouts, and inter-object relations. The fine-grained bank retains selected patch features that capture small objects, scene text, and other localized details that would otherwise be suppressed by regional aggregation. Together, these banks provide a compact yet scale-complementary visual representation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">While the three banks determine <em id="S3.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">which scales</em> of evidence are retained, the accompanying text determines <em id="S3.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">which content</em> is most relevant. Accordingly, MGVB conditions token selection in the regional and fine-grained banks on the available textual context <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">R</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> be a candidate region with pooled representation <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">r</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> be a patch feature associated with region <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{k(j)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">R</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">k</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{k(j)}</annotation></semantics></math>. Their relevance scores are computed as</p>
<table id="S3.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{k}^{r}=f_{r}(r_{k},x_{\mathrm{global}},c),\qquad a_{j}^{f}=f_{f}(x_{j},r_{k(j)},c)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">a</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">r</mi></msubsup><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">f</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">r</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">r</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">k</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">global</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">c</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">a</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">f</mi></msubsup><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">f</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">f</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">r</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">k</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">j</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">c</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{k}^{r}=f_{r}(r_{k},x_{\mathrm{global}},c),\qquad a_{j}^{f}=f_{f}(x_{j},r_{k(j)},c),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{\mathrm{global}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">global</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{\mathrm{global}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the global image representation, and <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">f</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">f</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> are learnable scoring functions. The top-ranked regions and patches are retained under budgets <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">B</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">B</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">f</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{f}</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. For instance, a question concerning a small chart label favors the corresponding local patches, whereas a question about the overall trend emphasizes the chart structure. Importantly, this context-aware selection only reallocates capacity within a shared representation; it introduces neither task-specific visual encoders nor separate backbone branches.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">MGVB follows the same selection principle across the three capabilities whenever visual input is present. The context <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> is instantiated by the text accompanying the image, such as a generation instruction, a retrieval query or caption, or a decision schema and its criteria. If no text is available, MGVB uses a query-independent context <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{\emptyset}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">c</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{\emptyset}</annotation></semantics></math>, ensuring that indexed representations do not depend on future queries. Finally, each retained token is augmented with granularity and spatial-position embeddings to encode its scale and spatial origin before being passed to the shared backbone.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">3.2  Unified Listwise Knowledge Distillation</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Retrieval and generation corpora provide complementary but typically unpaired forms of supervision. Retrieval examples contain relevance annotations but no reference responses, whereas generation examples provide target sequences without candidate-level relevance labels. A straightforward way to bridge this gap would be to annotate each example for both capabilities. As discussed in Section <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Conflicts Under Shared Capacity ‣ 2. Unified Multimodal Models: Formulation and Tensions ‣ WePM: Hierarchical Conflict Reconciliation for Unified MLLMs Unified Pocket Models for In-App Multimodal Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>, however, such cross-capability annotation is not only expensive but can also be fundamentally ambiguous. For example, a retrieval query such as “a small red flower” specifies meaningful relevance relations but admits many valid continuations rather than a unique generation target. Assigning one pseudo-response as the ground truth would impose an arbitrary interpretation on the query.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To address this supervision conflict, we introduce <em id="S3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Unified Listwise Knowledge Distillation</em>, which transfers soft teacher preferences instead of constructing unique hard targets for missing annotations. ULKD retains the native supervision available in each corpus while supplementing partially annotated inputs with capability-specific distributional guidance. In the present formulation, ULKD bridges the representation and generation supervision spaces; the decision path continues to use its native schema-conditioned typed objective.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">ULKD places retrieval and generation distillation within a common distribution-matching framework using two frozen capability-specific teachers. At each generation step, the choice set is the vocabulary, <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{gen}}=\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">𝒜</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">gen</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">𝒱</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{gen}}=\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math>, whereas retrieval defines a distribution over the candidate list, <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{emb}}=\mathcal{C}(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">𝒜</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">emb</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">𝒞</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{emb}}=\mathcal{C}(q)</annotation></semantics></math>. In both cases, the teacher provides relative preferences over the corresponding choice set, and the student minimizes a KL divergence to the teacher distribution. This formulation preserves multiple plausible alternatives instead of collapsing supervision into a single hard token, response, or positive candidate.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">For generation, directly assigning a pseudo-response to an open-ended retrieval query would impose one arbitrary interpretation as the target. ULKD instead performs on-policy distillation along trajectories sampled from the student itself <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">57</a>]</cite>. Let <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{emb}}^{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">𝒟</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">emb</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">q</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{emb}}^{q}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the query marginal of the retrieval corpus. For each query prompt <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, the student samples a continuation <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{y}\sim p_{S}(\cdot\mid q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">^</mo></mover><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">∼</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">p</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">S</mi></msub><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">(</mo><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" lspace="0em" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" lspace="0em" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}\sim p_{S}(\cdot\mid q)</annotation></semantics></math>, and the generation teacher evaluates every visited prefix:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="S3.SS2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Unlike sequence-level pseudo-labeling, this objective does not designate any complete continuation as uniquely correct. Instead, it aligns the student’s token distribution with the teacher on states induced by the student’s own policy, thereby providing generation supervision precisely along the trajectories encountered at inference time.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">For retrieval, the embedding teacher and student score the same candidate set <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">𝒞</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}(q)</annotation></semantics></math>. Their listwise distributions can be written together as</p>
<table id="S3.Ex10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p5.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">τ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">τ</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">S</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{S}</annotation></semantics></math> are temperature parameters. ULKD transfers both the teacher’s relative ordering over candidates and its instance-level representation. Specifically, a learnable projection <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> maps teacher embeddings into the student space:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex11" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex11X"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

stretchy="false">(</mo><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" lspace="0em" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" lspace="0em" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo <td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.Ex11Xa"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p5.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{\mathrm{opd}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">η</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">opd</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{\mathrm{opd}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{\mathrm{rank}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">η</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">rank</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{\mathrm{rank}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{\mathrm{repr}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">η</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">repr</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{\mathrm{repr}}</annotation></semantics></math> control the three distillation terms.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">During training, ULKD forms an auxiliary supervision stream alongside the original generation and retrieval objectives, while decision remains optimized with its native typed loss. Generation examples retain their standard token-level supervision, and retrieval examples retain their hard contrastive supervision through the last-state embedding readout. For a retrieval query, ULKD additionally samples an on-policy continuation and obtains token-level guidance from the generation teacher, while the embedding teacher transfers candidate-level ranking preferences and instance-level representations. ULKD therefore enriches task-specific data with complementary soft supervision without replacing their native objectives, requiring exhaustively paired annotations, or imposing a unique response on an open-ended query.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">3.3  Stable and Efficient Multitask Optimization</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The magnitude conflict identified in Section <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Conflicts Under Shared Capacity ‣ 2. Unified Multimodal Models: Formulation and Tensions ‣ WePM: Hierarchical Conflict Reconciliation for Unified MLLMs Unified Pocket Models for In-App Multimodal Intelligence" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> arises because the effective influence of each task depends jointly on its native gradient scale, loss coefficient, and exposure frequency. A multitask optimizer must therefore determine not only how strongly each task is weighted, but also how often it contributes to the shared update. Adaptive weighting methods such as Fast Adaptive Multitask Optimization (FAMO) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite> adjust task coefficients according to recent loss reduction. For heterogeneous objectives, however, short-term loss progress need not reflect the desired trade-off in downstream capability, and estimating such progress requires post-update loss re-evaluation and additional forward passes. Moreover, adaptive coefficients regulate only one component of task influence; the exposure assigned to each task remains a separate design choice. We therefore introduce <em id="S3.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Stable and Efficient Multitask Optimization</em>, which explicitly specifies both task weighting and task exposure while executing the resulting joint update through memory-efficient sequential gradient accumulation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Formally, let <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{T}=\{\mathrm{emb},\mathrm{gen},\mathrm{dec}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">𝒯</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">emb</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">gen</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">dec</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{T}=\{\mathrm{emb},\mathrm{gen},\mathrm{dec}\}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the representation, generation, and decision tasks. For task <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\mathcal{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">∈</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">𝒯</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\mathcal{T}</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{i,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">ℬ</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{i,t}</annotation></semantics></math> be the set of batches assigned to logical update <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{i,t}=|\mathcal{B}_{i,t}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">n</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">t</mi></mrow></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">=</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">ℬ</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">t</mi></mrow></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{i,t}=|\mathcal{B}_{i,t}|</annotation></semantics></math> determined by a predefined exposure schedule derived from the task-pool sizes. For each batch <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{i,b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC" mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">i</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FBFCFC;" mathbackground="#FBFCFC">b</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{i,b}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the task-native loss after the corresponding per-query, per-token, or per-decision-instance reduction. SEMO defines the logical-update objective as</p>
